description: TELEMETRY with ENCRYPTED set. payload_hex is a REAL AES-128-GCM ciphertext and tag, not a placeholder: it was produced with the Python `cryptography` package, and the key, nonce, AAD and plaintext are all published in the "aead" block below so any implementation can reproduce the exact octets as a cross-platform interoperability check. btp::decode() does not verify the tag (see test-vectors/v2/README.md); this vector proves the framing only -- version 2 selected automatically by ENCRYPTED, correct payload_size, envelope CRC over header plus ciphertext plus tag. flags=0x0002 has bits 2-3 (CIPHER_ID) clear, which is the normative encoding for AES-128-GCM.

aead.cipher_id_note: Normative value of the CIPHER_ID sub-field (bits 2-3 of flags, mask 0x000C) for AES-128-GCM. It matches bits 2-3 of the flags value above.
aead.key_note: Fixed, public, sequential test key, documented only so this vector can be reproduced. NEVER use in production: a real key never travels on the wire and is never written down in the clear.
aead.nonce_construction: source_id || boot_id || sequence, each 4 octets little-endian (btp::aead_nonce). Derivable from the frame fields above; spelled out here only for convenience.
aead.aad_construction: The 36 octets btp::encode_header() writes for this header, with the version octet already 2 because ENCRYPTED is set. Derivable from the frame fields above; spelled out here only for convenience.
aead.reproduction_note: payload_hex is the cipher's output over (nonce, plaintext, aad); the library appends the 16-octet tag, which is exactly the order the logical payload requires.
